bank.q: Consider the following statements linking the Preamble to the rights chapter:
s: Secularism entered the Preamble by the same amendment that inserted Articles 48A and 51A.
S. R. Bommai held secularism to be a basic feature.
The Preamble is itself an independent source of enforceable rights.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — the 42nd Amendment of 1976 inserted the word secular, Article 48A and Part IVA alike. The Preamble confers no independently enforceable rights.

bank.q: Match List I (right) with List II (article it is anchored in):
pairs: D. Duty to protect the environment
bank.e: Privacy sits in Articles 21 and 19 after Puttaswamy; unions in 19(1)(c); minority institutions in 30(1); the environmental duty in 51A(g).

bank.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Indra Sawhney barred reservation in promotions
Puttaswamy overruled Kharak Singh on privacy
Shayara Bano held triple talaq to be an essential religious practice
Pramati Trust exempted minority institutions from the RTE Act
bank.e: Shayara Bano held the opposite — triple talaq is not essential to Islam, and was therefore unprotected by Article 25.

bank.as: Both the Essential Religious Practices doctrine and the Basic Structure Doctrine are judicial creations with no textual anchor.
bank.rs: Each gives courts the power to decide what is fundamental to something they did not author — a religion in one case, the Constitution in the other.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The parallel is exactly why both attract the same criticism of counter-majoritarian overreach.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: Shirur Mutt (1954) → Maneka Gandhi (1978) → Indra Sawhney (1992) → Puttaswamy (2017).

bank.q: Consider the following statements on amendments that responded to judgments:
s: The First Amendment inserted Article 15(4) after Champakam Dorairajan.
The 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5) after P. A. Inamdar.
The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A along with the eleventh Fundamental Duty.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they show the recurring pattern of Parliament amending the Constitution in direct response to judicial holdings.

bank.q: Which of the following pairs of doctrines both require the State to justify a restriction as proportionate?
o: Essential Religious Practices and reasonable classification
Puttaswamy's privacy test and the reasonableness test under Article 19
bank.e: Puttaswamy imported an explicit proportionality standard, and reasonableness under Article 19 has long required a proximate nexus and the least restrictive means — as in V. G. Row and S. Rangarajan.

bank.q: All of the following are non-justiciable EXCEPT:
o: Article 44, on a uniform civil code
Article 48A, on protection of the environment
bank.e: Article 30(1) is a Fundamental Right and directly enforceable. The other three are Directive Principles or Fundamental Duties.

bank.as: Article 21 has become the most litigated provision of the Constitution.
bank.rs: Maneka Gandhi converted procedure established by law into a substantive due process standard, opening the article to expansive reading.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — from livelihood and shelter to privacy, climate and dignity in dying, almost every new right runs through Article 21.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about restrictions on rights:
s: Article 33 permits Parliament to restrict the rights of members of the armed forces and associated staff.
Article 19(4) governs restrictions on the freedom of association.
Article 25 is subject to public order, morality and health.
bank.e: All three are correct. Article 33 was applied in O. K. Achudan Nair, Article 19(4) in V. G. Row, and the internal limitations in Article 25 underpin the entire ERP jurisprudence.
